summary: The article examines the global boom in health and wellness products and argues that growth in emerging markets is uneven. It cites infrastructural and economic divides, cultural mismatch with Western paradigms, regulatory weaknesses and the digital divide as barriers. It ends on a hopeful note about local innovators aligning products with regional needs, and calls for collaboration among governments, businesses and communities.
one_line: Health and wellness markets are booming globally, but emerging markets face cost, cultural, regulatory and digital barriers, with local innovation offering a path forward.
key_facts: A Markets & Markets report published September 15, 2023 projects the global health and wellness market will reach $6 trillion by 2025, with emerging markets contributing a considerable portion.
Health and wellness consumption has historically been a Western phenomenon, strong in the United States and Western Europe.
India, Brazil and South Africa are cited as emerging markets that have introduced a new demographic of wellness enthusiasts.
Market analyst Dr. Maureen Njoki, interviewed October 6, 2023, said infrastructural inadequacies and economic disparities are the bedrock of challenges in emerging markets.
Startups 'ZestAlive' in Nairobi and 'VivaVitae' in Rio de Janeiro struggle to gain traction because high production costs lead to prices beyond the average consumer.
Sociologist Dr. Ramon Esteban's research, dated November 12, 2023, identifies a cultural mismatch between Westerncentric wellness paradigms and local traditions, lowering uptake.
International wellness brands pushing 'superfoods' or supplements can seem alien or even neocolonial in cultures where traditional medicine and community-based healthcare prevail.

Independent health policy consultant James Williams said in a December 21, 2023 webinar that the lack of comprehensive regulation for alternative health products leads to counterfeit and low-quality goods.
Regulatory problems in emerging markets include stringent import restrictions, convoluted bureaucratic processes and inconsistent quality standards.
A September 2023 UN Conference on Trade and Development survey reported a gap in digital readiness between emerging markets and developed nations.
Limited internet access and digital literacy keep many people in emerging markets from using e-commerce channels for wellness products.
HealthForAll, founded by entrepreneur Priya Singh in Kolkata, incorporates Ayurvedic principles into accessible wellness products.
The article calls for supporting local innovation, fostering an inclusive digital landscape and aligning products with cultural sensibilities.
